extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers, applicants, and NIH staff involved in R01-style grant review
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance describing the simplified peer review framework for R01-style research project grant applications effective Jan 25, 2025, reorganizing review criteria into three Factors and an Overall Impact score. Useful for reviewers scoring applications and applicants preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (old criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance — one of the five pre-2025 criteria; reviewers scored this on a 1-9 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically evaluated the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress in the field; listed as part of the old five criteria prior to the Jan 2025 reform. (Now combined into Factor 1: Importance of the Research.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (old criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) — one of the five pre-2025 criteria; reviewers scored this on a 1-9 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically evaluated the qualifications, suitability, and track record of the PI and key personnel. (Now combined into Factor 3: Expertise and Resources and evaluated as a sufficiency check rather than a scored item.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (old criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation — one of the five pre-2025 criteria; reviewers scored this on a 1-9 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically assessed novel conceptual approaches, methods, or technologies. (Now folded into Factor 1: Importance of the Research.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (old criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach — one of the five pre-2025 criteria; reviewers scored this on a 1-9 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically covered strategy, methodology, analyses, and feasibility. (Many Approach-related items are now part of Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (old criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment — one of the five pre-2025 criteria; reviewers scored this on a 1-9 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically assessed institutional support, resources, and facilities. (Now incorporated into Factor 3: Expertise and Resources and treated as a sufficiency assessment.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (scored 1-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines Significance and Innovation. Reviewers evaluate the importance of the proposed research in context of current scientific challenges and opportunities; whether the research advances knowledge in the field broadly; and novelty of concepts, approaches, methodologies, or instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored on a 1-9 scale. Focus is on the science itself — its importance, potential to advance the field, and novelty. This factor explicitly merges the historic Significance and Innovation dimensions into a single scored factor to concentrate assessment on research content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (scored 1-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines the former Approach criterion plus previously-separate ARC (Approach/Research Conduct) items. Reviewers evaluate whether the strategy, methodology, and analyses are rigorous and feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored on a 1-9 scale. Specific elements called out for evaluation include: strategy, methodology, analyses; inclusion criteria and coding for clinical/translational research; study timelines for clinical trials; plans for valid design and analysis of Phase III clinical trials; scientific premise and rigor of prior research; consideration of biological variables (sex, age, etc.); and authentication of key biological/chemical resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (sufficiency check; not numerically scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines Investigator and Environment into a non-scored assessment of whether the project team and institutional resources are sufficient to conduct the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated for SUFFICIENCY rather than with a 1-9 score. Reviewers select from a dropdown: 'Appropriate' (no comments required) or 'Additional expertise/resources needed' (comments required identifying gaps). The goal is to separate capability/resource considerations from scored judgments about the science to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Score (holistic, scored 1-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single, holistic score that integrates Factors 1, 2, and 3 to reflect the reviewers' overall assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retains the historical 1-9 scoring scale. Reviewers produce this score after considering the scored Factors (1 and 2) and the sufficiency determination in Factor 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items removed from peer reviewer evaluation (administratively reviewed instead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the reform, certain items are no longer evaluated by peer reviewers and are instead administratively reviewed by NIH staff before funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items explicitly listed as removed from peer review: Applications from Foreign Organizations; Select Agents work; Resource Sharing Plans. These items remain part of the administrative compliance and policy review but are not to be scored by peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and design goals for the restructuring
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy goals that guided the reorganization: reduce reviewer bias, address documented racial disparities, reduce reviewer cognitive load, and increase focus on the science itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH cites evidence informing the change: Witteman 2019 (PI-focused criteria amplified gender bias), Erosheva 2020 (criterion scores carry the disparity), and Pier 2018 (reviewers cannot reliably distinguish granular scores). These findings motivated moving Investigator/Environment to a non-scored sufficiency check, reducing dimensionality from five scored criteria to two scored Factors plus a sufficiency check, and simplifying reviewers' task.
